title: Gear-Driven Spectral Dispersion Calibrator
description: A mechanical chemistry apparatus where interlocking gears drive a prism dispersion system. The user must rotate gear assemblies to precisely angle the prism, adjust beam intensity and wavelength inputs, and calibrate spectral output bands while obeying energy conservation — with full undo/redo support for each adjustment step.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a gear-driven spectral dispersion calibrator in a chemistry lab setting. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: place the DispersionTest model (a prism/dispersion apparatus) at center-right of the scene, and the gears model at center-left, mechanically linked via a visible shaft (a simple cylinder). Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to 45-degree vertical arc. Lighting: warm directional light simulating a lab lamp from above-left, plus soft ambient light with a slight blue tint. Add a subtle grid floor and a dark lab-bench colored plane beneath the models.

Interaction system (10-14 steps, L6 difficulty): The user clicks and drags on the gears model to rotate it; this mechanically rotates the prism in the DispersionTest model proportionally (multi-input coupling). Provide three HTML slider controls overlaid on the canvas: (1) Beam Intensity (0-100%), (2) Input Wavelength (380nm-780nm), (3) Gear Ratio selector (1:1, 2:1, 3:1). A colored beam (RaycasterLine or TubeGeometry) enters the prism from the left, disperses into spectral bands exiting right. The output spectral energy must equal input energy (conservation law): increasing one output band must decrease others proportionally. Display a real-time energy bar showing total input vs total output; if they diverge, flash a red warning.

Implement an undo/redo stack (minimum 14 states) tracking gear rotation angle, slider values, and prism orientation. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo, Ctrl+Y for redo, and show small undo/redo buttons on screen. Each gear drag completion, slider change, or gear-ratio switch counts as one recorded step. Show a step counter (e.g., 'Step 7/12'). The task is complete when the user has matched a target spectral distribution shown as a ghost overlay on the output side, requiring at least 10 deliberate adjustments. Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth gear tooth meshing animation synced to prism rotation. All UI uses a semi-transparent dark panel styled for a chemistry lab aesthetic.
